# run_gladiator { #turtle_widget.run_gladiator }

```python
turtle_widget.run_gladiator(
    strategy_a,
    strategy_b,
    *,
    max_rounds=500,
    canvas_size=500,
    hitbox_radius=15,
    arena_margin=60,
    homes=None,
    colors=('blue', 'red'),
    speed=6,
    show_scoreboard=True,
    autoshow=True,
)
```

Run a step-based, alternating gladiator duel and return the outcome.

Two turtles share one canvas, spawned on opposite walls facing each other. Each
round, ``strategy_a(a, b)`` is called, then ``strategy_b(b, a)`` -- each call
should perform **one bounded action** (e.g. sense, maybe turn, move a short
step), not loop to completion. After each call the harness checks whether that
turtle's move rammed the other's ``hitbox``; the first to do so wins. Running out
of ``max_rounds`` without a ram is a draw.

## Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

<code>[**strategy_a**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[callable](`callable`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   Each called as ``strategy(me, opponent)`` once per round.

<code>[**strategy_b**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[callable](`callable`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   Each called as ``strategy(me, opponent)`` once per round.

<code>[**max_rounds**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[int](`int`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [500]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Round cap before a draw is declared. ``0`` ends immediately in a draw without calling either strategy -- useful for inspecting the initial arena. Default 500.

<code>[**canvas_size**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[int](`int`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [500]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Side length of the (square) shared canvas. Default 500.

<code>[**hitbox_radius**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[float](`float`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [15]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Collision radius for both turtles -- see :func:`Turtle.hitbox`. Default 15.

<code>[**arena_margin**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[float](`float`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [60]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Distance from each side wall to that turtle's default home, when ``homes`` is not given. Must satisfy ``0 < arena_margin < canvas_size / 2``. Default 60.

<code>[**homes**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [tuple of two (x, y, heading) tuples]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Explicit spawn points, overriding the auto-computed opposite-walls, facing-each-other default.

<code>[**colors**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [tuple of two (str or None)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [(\'blue\', \'red\')]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Pen colours for A and B, for telling them apart. Default ``("blue", "red")``.

<code>[**speed**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[int](`int`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [6]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Turtle drawing speed. Default 6.

<code>[**show_scoreboard**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[bool](`bool`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [True]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   If True (default), write the outcome on the canvas when the duel ends.

<code>[**autoshow**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[bool](`bool`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [True]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Passed straight through to the internal turtles. Default True; pass False for headless use such as tests.

## Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

<code>[]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[GladiatorResult](`turtle_widget.games.GladiatorResult`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   The outcome -- see its field descriptions for details.

## Notes {.doc-section .doc-section-notes}

Both turtles get ``on_collision(handler, walls=True, turtles=True)``. A wall hit
(``obstacle.kind == "wall"``) truncates that turtle's move to the arena boundary
-- a wasted action -- but does **not** end the duel; only ``obstacle.kind ==
"turtle"`` does. Neither turtle collides with drawn trail.
